subject: Requesting runbook window + data ingest slot before customer demo
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting runbook window + data ingest slot before customer demo

Team —

SaaSCo just confirmed the public demo for next Thursday, but they recently flagged travel for their VP and asked for an earlier dry-run. We should push the public demo by one business day to get a proper prep/dry-run. I need help coordinating the following before we confirm with the customer: 

- Reserve a 90-minute dry-run window (internal + customer) during which we can run the end-to-end flow with their sample dataset.
- Prepare a concise runbook for the session (steps, fallback, required credentials).
- Make the sample dataset ingest-ready on the staging cluster and provide ingest commands.
- Ship the prompt sets and workload traces we'll use during the demo so CS and the customer can validate outputs.

Can each of you own one of these? Rishi — can you propose 2 candidate windows (PST) that keep the demo on Fri/Mon timeframe? Hannah — runbook draft. Marcus — get the staging ingest prepped and an ingest script. I’ll loop the customer after we have windows and the runbook.

Attachments I plan to send to the customer: runbook stub, sample dataset, and ingest script.

Thanks — Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requesting runbook window + data ingest slot before customer demo

On Fri, Oct 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> SaaSCo just confirmed the public demo for next Thursday...

Thanks, Olga — I can take the scheduling and will propose slots. High-level notes:

- We should offer one full-day option (two adjacent 90-min blocks) and one compact option (single 90-min block) in case their VP has limited time.
- Candidate windows (PST):
  * Option A: Fri Oct 9, 10:30–12:00 (PST) — gives us time for a Fri dry-run and public demo Mon Oct 12.
  * Option B: Mon Oct 12, 13:00–14:30 (PST) — if they prefer the demo same day as VP availability.

I’ll hold both tentative in my calendar and can share a calendar poll. Marcus/Hannah — can you confirm feasibility for those windows (staging capacity, runbook availability) by EOD today? I’ll draft a short email to Alex (SaaSCo) with the two options.

—Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@saasco.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kevin Wu <kevin.wu@finlytics.io>
Date: Sat, 04 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requesting runbook window + data ingest slot before customer demo

Hi Olga / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Our VP is traveling but can be on a short window Friday morning. The team prefers a single 90-minute slot. Of your options, Option A (Fri Oct 9, 10:30–12:00 PST) works best. A couple of asks from my side before we lock: 

1) We need the ingest steps and file manifest so our security folks can pre-approve the sample upload. Please include required IAM roles and an expected size estimate.
2) Can you provide the prompt sets you plan to run and a short note on what success looks like for each prompt? Our product team wants to validate fidelity against our internal traces.
3) If possible, could you give the team a 15-minute readout window 24 hours before the dry-run for a quick alignment (internal only)?

If you can share the runbook + ingest script and the prompts today, I’ll route to security. We’ll send a calendar invite once we get the artifacts.

Best —
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Integrations, SaaSCo
alex.j@saasco.com | +1 (415) 867-2345
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@saasco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requesting runbook window + data ingest slot before customer demo

Thanks Alex — that works. Confirming the dry-run: Fri Oct 9, 10:30–12:00 PST (90 minutes). We’ll also hold a 15-minute internal readout on Thu Oct 8 at 09:30 PST as requested.

What we sent (attachments & links):
- redwood_demo_runbook_v1.pdf — step-by-step agenda, rollback steps, MLE/CS contacts
- saasco_sample_dataset_v03.csv — partial sample (synthesized) and manifest (size ~22 MB)
- ingest_steps.sh — one-line commands to stage the data to our staging bucket; requires a service account with storage.write role (details in runbook)
- prompt_set_examples.txt — the exact prompts and short acceptance criteria per prompt

Links: runbook and artifacts are in this shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-demo-runbooks
Staging runbook (internal): https://share.redwood.ai/runbooks/saasco-onboarding
Calendar: I’ll send the official invite once I get a thumbs up from your side; tentative hold added here: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=SaAsCo-demo-proposed-slot

Marcus — you confirmed staging capacity earlier — please ensure the ingest path is writable and the lightweight ingest container is pre-pulled on the nodes. Hannah — please iterate on the runbook (shorten the troubleshooting section to a 1-page checklist). Rishi — I’ll ask Ops to set an internal hold on Fri morning.

Alex — if anything changes with VP travel, let us know immediately. Otherwise, we’ll expect the calendar invite and will prepare the dry-run checklist.

Thanks —
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Attachments: redwood_demo_runbook_v1.pdf, saasco_sample_dataset_v03.csv, ingest_steps.sh, prompt_set_examples.txt
